statement: For $x\\neq 0$ let $f(x)=\\tfrac{x^{2}+4}{2x}$. (i) Show that $f(x)=f(4/x)$ for $x>0$. (ii) Find the minimum value of $f(x)$ for $x>0$ and where it occurs. (iii) Hence solve $f(x)=\\tfrac52$.
solution: (i) $f(4/x)=\\tfrac{(16/x^{2})+4}{8/x}=\\tfrac{16+4x^{2}}{8x}=\\tfrac{4+x^{2}}{2x}=f(x)$. (ii) $f(x)=\\tfrac{x}{2}+\\tfrac{2}{x}\\ge 2\\sqrt{\\tfrac{x}{2}\\cdot\\tfrac{2}{x}}=2$ by AM-GM, equality when $\\tfrac{x}{2}=\\tfrac{2}{x}$, i.e. $x^{2}=4$, so $x=2$ ($x>0$). Minimum $2$ at $x=2$. (iii) $\\tfrac{x}{2}+\\tfrac{2}{x}=\\tfrac52\\Rightarrow x^{2}-5x+4=0\\Rightarrow x=1$ or $4$. By (i) $f(1)=f(4)=\\tfrac52$.
hints: Apply AM-GM or calculus for the minimum.
